newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close mixed to limit down.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close mixed to limit down.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed down the $10.00 per tbf limit in November on pressure from weak cash and technicals. Most back months followed on spillover selling, traders said.
November ended limit down at $329.40 per tbf with other months off $8.40 to up $1.10 per tbf. January was off $8.40 at $346.60 per tbf.

Futures were under pressure from the start on the continued weak tone to cash lumber. Sell stops were touched off under $335, basis Novemberwhich added to early weakness and prompted pressure down to the limit, traders said.

Cash lumber prices are expected to continue declining as retailer demand remains sparse. Analysts see spruce falling to $350 or lower before encouraging demand, especially at current production levels.
"Production has outpaced demand the past couple of weeks," said lumber analyst Paul Court.
Prudential Securities and Saul Stone notably sold on the decline with long January/short November spreads adding to the nearby loss, pit sources added.
